relevance_note: Single case report of an infant with a de novo heterozygous TNFAIP3 frameshift: "revealing a heterozygous mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene at chr6:138200458–138200459, NM_001270508.2:c.1876_1877del (p.Leu626ValfsTer45)".
method_note: Read the paper manually; this JSON was assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory, values typed from my reading and every span checked verbatim against the Markdown. Individuals: the index infant ('patient', rule 5); his father and mother (both Sanger-tested negative, Figure 4 legend); two previously published HA20 patients described in the Discussion with individual-level facts (Iwasa (12): sex, age, features; Zhang (7): onset, features), labelled by rule 4 using the citation as printed. The two paternal half-brothers ('his two half-brothers had no similar medical history') were neither tested nor described as affected, so they were left out of scope. No variant rows for the two literature patients: the text gives no variant for them (the reference list title of ref 7 mentions a deletion, but the text does not tie it to the person). Parents get no variant rows because they do not carry the variant. Table 1 (laboratory values): the legend says bold values are abnormal; abnormal (bold) values were recorded as observed with the legend quoted as a second span. Non-bold values and '(-)' cells were not used as exclusions, because the paper does not define '(-)' or non-bold as negative/normal. 'Cardiopulmonary examination was normal' and 'No abnormalities were detected in the anus or external genitalia' were recorded as written (whole-exam negatives) and exclude nothing more specific (genital ulcers, serositis stay not reported). Enterovirus: negative during the first hospitalisation but detected in one later diarrhoea episode; both rows emitted (different episodes, not treated as a contradiction). Checklist: 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' left not reported although haemoglobin was low and Coombs-C3 was (++), because the authors do not call it autoimmune cytopenia; 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' left not reported (diarrhoea only; endoscopy declined). Liver and spleen palpable below the costal margin recorded as stated, without an HPO candidate, because the authors do not call them enlarged. Minor inconsistencies in the paper: Table 1 'Creatinine' repeats the BUN value and unit (3.03 mmol/L); Table 1 red blood cell reference range (4.3–14.2 × 10^12/L) looks copied from WBC; the abstract protein string has a space ('p. Leu626ValfsTer45').
